questionText: How do you design API error responses for good developer experience?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can pair the correct HTTP status with a stable Problem Details body, design useful validation extensions, and keep sensitive diagnostics in protected logs.
outOfScope: Treating English detail text as a machine code

claims.statement: The actual HTTP response status carries the protocol outcome; a Problem Details status member is advisory and generators must keep it equal to the HTTP status they send.
RFC 9457 defines type as the problem-class identifier, title as a short summary of that type, detail as an occurrence-specific explanation, and instance as an identifier for the occurrence.
Problem Details permits extension members, and clients should use defined extensions instead of parsing the human-readable detail string for machine decisions.
Problem responses can expose implementation details if carelessly generated, so stack traces, database text, secrets, and internal topology should remain outside the public error body.
Spring MVC supplies ProblemDetail and ErrorResponse support and allows controller advice to centralize exception-to-response handling, while the application still chooses domain-safe mappings.

examples.title: RFC 9457 validation problem with application extensions

validation.command: Parse the fenced response JSON and verify status 422, application/problem+json, standard members, and extension-member types
validation.expected: Valid JSON with consistent HTTP/body status and no internal diagnostics

visuals.title: Protocol status, standard Problem Details members, application extensions, and log correlation

notes: The errors and correlationId members in the example are application-defined extensions, not RFC 9457 standard members.

review.notes: Standard member semantics and security cautions were checked against RFC 9457; Spring support was checked against the managed Spring reference.
